entries.name: The Greatest
entries.description: “Cross” creator Ben Watkins sets his talented sights on the life of Cassius Clay as the promising young boxer takes his first steps to becoming the cultural icon Muhammad Ali. It's the first authorized portrayal of Ali's life and career, and a massive opportunity for newcomer Jaalen Best as Clay. — Arno

entries.name: Black Doves
entries.description: Coming off the deadly Christmas finale, Season 2 promises even higher stakes and bigger explosions as Keira Knightley and Ben Whishaw return as undercover spy Helen and hitman Sam, navigating even deadlier waters as Helen's husband prepares to become Prime Minister. The darkly humorous thriller makes some stellar additions to the cast, with Ambika Mod, Babou Ceesay, and Neve Campbell joining the chaos. — Vanessa

entries.name: Wild Horse Nine
entries.description: Few filmmakers combine rich character work, biting humor, and an evocative sense of place quite like Martin McDonagh. John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell are pitch-perfect as two aging CIA operatives who leave 1973 Chile for a holiday on Easter Island to see “the big heads.” But what begins as an odd-couple getaway gradually becomes a reckoning with friendship, mortality, and lives spent doing terrible things. Against the remote beauty of Rapa Nui and its ancient monuments, McDonagh turns their rueful romp into something darkly funny and unexpectedly tender: a story about two men confronting what, if anything, they’ll leave behind. — Matt

entries.name: Godzilla Minus Zero
entries.description: Godzilla Minus Zero looks to build on its predecessor’s successes by picking up two years after the events of Godzilla Minus One. As postwar Japan is in rebuilding mode, the Shikishima family quickly realizes they’re going to face a second round with Godzilla. And this time, the King of the Monsters will have to defend its title against King Ghidorah, the towering, dragon-like Titan that has become a central figure in the current Warner Bros. MonsterVerse movies but hasn’t been seen in a Toho production in 25 years. Writer-director and visual effects titan Takashi Yamazaki returns for the sequel, which was filmed in IMAX for our collective pleasure. It’s also the first Godzilla movie to earn an R rating! — Arno

entries.name: Dexter: Resurrection
entries.description: Everyone’s favorite serial killer with a heart of gold is back for a second season of this hit spin-off series, and this time Dexter Morgan is taking on the most frightening foe of them all: a mid-life crisis. Uma Thurman returns as Charley, a former Special Ops agent who left her role as right-hand man to billionaire Leon Prater at the end of Season 1. But lest we make it seem like Dexter’s only dilemma is middle age, let us introduce two new serial killers into the mix. Brian Cox and Dan Stevens join the cast for the new 10-episode arc as the New York Ripper and the Five Borough Killer and are sure to make dear Dexter’s life much more complicated. — Adrienne

entries.name: The Gilded Age
entries.description: Season 4 of this hit HBO Max series looks like it will be a story of operatic proportions. Bertha (Carrie Coon) finally has the social status she's been craving for so long, but can she and her family withstand the pressures of her success? With Agnes (Christine Baranski) looking for a way back on top, and Marian (Louisa Jacobson) and Peggy (Denée Benton) striving for more stable lives, New York's high society is in for eight episodes of twists and turns. Come for the delicious drama, stay for the insane supporting cast, including Cynthia Nixon, Taissa Farmiga, Dylan Baker, Brian Stokes Mitchell, Jim Gaffigan, and Bill Camp, among others. —Adrienne

entries.name: The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power
entries.detail: Season 3 premieres November 11 on Prime Video
entries.description: Sauron continues his ascent in Season 3, as "Rings of Power" brings some major events from Tolkien's lore to the screen, including the war between the Elves and Sauron, and the forging of the One Ring (to rule them all). Jamie Campbell Bower joins "Rings of Power" in a pivotal role as Celeborn, the Elven lord and long-lost husband of Galadriel, who returns just in time for all hell to break loose. Start your binge-watch when the first four of eight episodes drop on Nov. 11. — Vanessa

entries.name: How to Rob a Bank
entries.description: Although this social media-heavy action-heist doesn't tread a lot of new ground, the cast is what's got us interested. The law-vs-outlaw divide pits Nicholas Hoult and Pete Davidson, leading the robbers with a message, against John C. Reilly and Zoë Kravitz, who try to take them down. And with David Leitch at the helm (Bullet Train, Deadpool 2, The Fall Guy), crazy stunts and over-the-top action are pretty much a given. — Vanessa

entries.name: Ebenezer
entries.description: Can 2026 Johnny Depp lure audiences to theaters with a dark themed holiday movie? If he had made Ebenenzer in, say, 1992 with Tim Burton, chances are we'd all own 4K copies of the film and pack theaters every year for a Christmastime revival. It’s tricky to predict how indie horror maven Ti West’s version of Charles Dickens’ A Christmas Carol will perform during its theatrical run, and what word of mouth will be like when opening weekend audiences decide if West’s interpretation, which certainly is not canon, is worth the cost of admission. But the movie could be more of a success in the Christmas Future. — Arno

entries.name: Victorian Psycho
entries.description: Resist the urge to make American Psycho comparisons with this new horror-comedy from Zachary Wigon (Sanctuary), which is likely to bring a few more belly laughs along with its mayhem. Based on screenwriter Virginia Feito’s novel of the same name, Victorian Psycho follows the possibly (definitely) insane (homicidal?) governess Winifred Notty (Maika Monroe) as she brings her unique set of skills to service the stuffy inhabitants of a remote gothic manor. Is all hell about to break loose? Yes. Are you going to have a great time watching it happen? Also yes. Will there be blood? As the Victorians might say, “Most assuredly.” — Adrienne

entries.name: Madden
entries.description: Polarizing filmmaker David O. Russell’s biopic of storied NFL coach John Madden will not address the rather barbaric tactics he used during his early tenure with the Oakland Raiders, something fans called out when the Madden trailer first dropped. The movie, which is skipping a theatrical release and going direct to Prime Video, will show a more sanitized version of how Madden turned the team into a dynasty before he broadened his cultural footprint first as an NFL commentator, then as the vision and voice behind his namesake video game franchise. It leaves in-the-know fans wondering: Why employ Nic Cage as Madden and Christian Bale as Raiders owner, Al Davis, in a calmed-down version of this story? The two stars who know a thing about volatility both on- and off-screen. — Arno

entries.name: The Altruists
entries.description: It could be serendipitous timing for “The Altruists” in the wake of the Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything becoming a cultural phenomenon. Julia Garner and Anthony Boyle co-star in this mini-series about convicted cryptocurrency felons Caroline Ellison and Sam Bankman-Fried. Expect a new wave of journalism about the duo, and seek out this summer’s New York Magazine story on Bankman-Fried to get the deepest dive on his life behind bars. The series is essentially mirroring “The Dropout,” since there's a torrent of Ellison/Bankman-Fried documentaries coming our way soon. — Arno

entries.name: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping
entries.description: The story of Haymitch Abernathy’s first Hunger Games has been completely eclipsed by the news that Katniss and Peeta will appear in the latest prequel, even though the movie is set more than two decades before the original trilogy (Suzanne Collins readers already know her fifth and maybe final Hunger Gs novel has a fast-forward section to the Team Peeta era). The return of Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson is a gift to fans and a coup for the franchise, which we sense will continue to live on, especially if the second prequel bests the first at the box office (which still matters in instances like this). Back to young Abernathy: The role is a score for Joseph Zada, who’s set himself up nicely after “We Were Liars.” — Arno

entries.name: Yellowjackets
entries.description: We’ll get to see exactly how many Yellowjackets make it back home to Wiskayok, NJ in the fourth and final season of the hit series that has been dinged, battered, and still beloved over the course of its previous three seasons. But things don’t necessarily get less brutal for the survivors back home; brace for a new murderous plot to be set into motion, as Molly Ringwald, June Squibb, and others bring to an end this fever dream for some permanently scarred teens. — Arno

entries.name: I Play Rocky
entries.description: Expect a fairly faithful adaptation of the creation of the film Rocky in this docudrama from director Peter Farrelly. Starring Anthony Ippolito as Sylvester Stallone, I Play Rocky follows a young artist’s unlikely journey from unknown actor to Hollywood success story. Stallone famously wrote the script for his Oscar-winning movie in just three days and then refused to sell it unless he was allowed to play the title role. I Play Rocky dramatizes those events into a movie that is already gathering positive press after its premiere at TIFF earlier this fall. — Adrienne

entries.name: Paper Tiger
entries.description: It's the cast that's turning heads with James Gray's crime drama about a pair of brothers who become entangled with the Russian mafia when they agree to a scheme that's too good to be true. Adam Driver and Miles Teller turn up the tension as the duped siblings, alongside Scarlett Johansson who plays Teller's terrorized wife in this period drama that is sure to raise your blood pressure. — Arno

entries.name: Percy Jackson and the Olympians
entries.detail: Season 3 premieres November 20 on Prime Video
entries.description: Season 3 of this much-loved reimagining of Greek mythology is bringing a darker tone to Percy and The Seven’s adventures. This time, the eight-episode season will adapt author Rick Riordan’s third book in the series, “The Titan’s Curse,” which leaves Percy to face the disappearance of Annabeth and the Great Prophecy that says one demigod child is fated to either raise Olympus to new heights or bring it crashing down to ruin. — Adrienne

entries.name: The Good Daughter
entries.description: Karin Slaughter might have her next TV moment this fall. The author, who has the hit series “Will Trent” to her credit, serves as showrunner here, overseeing the adaptation of her novel. The story concerns two estranged sisters (Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy) who reunite nearly 30 years after a traumatic childhood experience which left their mother dead and the rest of their family deeply fractured and traumatized. In their small town, which looks sort of like the world of “Task” (a compliment), another bone-chilling event makes their family history high-stakes headline news again. — Arno

entries.name: Hexed
entries.description: Disney has owned the Thanksgiving weekend box office the past two years with mega-franchise sequels Moana 2 and Zootopia 2, but this year the studio is placing its bets on an original animated feature Hexed. Hailee Steinfeld voices Billie Doe, a teen girl who discovers latent magical powers that lead her to Hexe, the magical realm of witches. As is customary, the voice cast is stacked with names that will mean more to parents than kids. — James

entries.name: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth
entries.description: Quentin Tarantino’s output as director will never match the voracious appetite for his films from movie fans. Thankfully, he’s enlisted David Fincher to direct the follow-up to Once Upon a Time in... Hollywood. Based on Tarantino’s script, this sequel catches up with stuntman Cliff Booth (Brad Pitt) eight years after the events of Once Upon a Time, now a “studio fixer” who gets mixed up with a new host of characters around Los Angeles (some seedy, some really seedy), including a talent agent (Elizabeth Debicki), a football star-turned-actor (Yahya Abdul-Mateen II), a TV star (Scott Caan) and his wife (Carla Gugino), and the return of Timothy Olyphant as Western star James Stacy. — James

entries.name: Focker-in-Law
entries.description: If there’s a formula for mainstream comedy success in 2026, it seems to be early 2000s nostalgia. The two biggest comedies at the box office this year have been The Devil Wears Prada 2 and Scary Movie. Cue Robert de Niro and Ben Stiller’s reunion in Focker-In-Law, the third sequel to 2000’s Meet the Parents and the first since 2010’s Little Fockers. This time around, the franchise gets an infusion of youth with the introduction of Ariana Grande, who plays foil to Stiller as his prospective daughter-in-law, soon to be wed to son Henry, played by rising star Skyler Gisondo (Primetime, Superman). — James

entries.name: Blade Runner 2099
entries.detail: Series premieres November 25 on Prime Video
entries.description: The sci-fi saga that started with Ridley Scott’s Blade Runner in 1982 and continued with Blade Runner 2049 in 2017 is getting a third installment this month with the miniseries “Blade Runner 2099.” Set half a century after the last film, the eight-episode season explores a future where replicants reign supreme and humans are reduced to second-class citizens. These two worlds are personified by Michelle Yeoh’s replicant Olwen and Hunter Schafter as Cora, a human fugitive forced to assume the identity of a replicant blade runner. Expect more high-bar aesthetics with this series as well, with showrunner Silka Luisa calling the show’s style “sunshine noir.” — Adrienne

entries.name: The Hunting Wives
entries.description: Where do you go after a killer has been revealed and there’s no apparent end to the bad behavior in the ritzy enclave of Maple Brook, Texas? We’ll find out over eight episodes as “The Hunting Wives” Season 2 picks up right after the events of Season 1 and dares to take a time jump into the future into a land that has not been traversed in Rebecca Cutter’s novels. Who knows what the terms and conditions of the frenemy alliance between Sophie (Brittany Snow) and Margo (Malin Akerman) will look like, but we do know “Widow’s Bay” legend and recent Emmy nominee Dale Dickey will add to the Season 2 fracas, and Netflix has already renewed the series for Season 3. — Arno
